claim.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Eur. Phys. J. C 83 (2023) 963

key_value.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

name: Top quark mass measured to 0.37 GeV

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.
significance.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

summary.plain: CMS weighed the top quark, the heaviest known elementary particle, to a precision of about two parts in a thousand.
summary.technical: 36.3 fb^-1 at 13 TeV, lepton+jets ttbar candidates, kinematic fit plus a profile likelihood over up to four observables: m_t = 171.77 +/- 0.37 GeV.

title: Measurement of the top quark mass using a profile likelihood approach with the lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
why_it_matters: The top quark mass enters the electroweak fit and the stability of the Higgs potential, so every improvement in its precision sharpens tests of the standard model.
